loadAudioFile:
Load audio from file.
Parameter values can be animated in response to the input from audio files.
The following formats are supported:
- *.wav (wave form audio format)
- *.ogg (Ogg Vorbis)
- *.flac (Free Lossless Audio Format)
- *.mp3 (MPEG II Audio Layer 3) - supported only under Linux
animsound_enable:
Enables Animation by Sound, which uses digital data from audio files to adjust parameter values obtained from the keyframe animation table.
The change in a parameter value can be in response to either the amplitude or the pitch of the sound sampled at each frame (independent from keyframes.)
There are two types of parameters in this program.   The first type can have negative values entered, the second type  cannot. It is important when animating a parameter of the second type, that the functions and settings used do not result in a negative number.
Animation by Sound can be used in combination with animation from the Keyframe table.
Example:
An object can be moving in a linear direction in respect to the keyframe animation table calculation, and at the same time have this movement responding to the audio.
animsound_additionfactor:
The value of animation of a parameter, is the sum of the sound value added to the parameter value (from the keyframe animation table):
animation = parameter_value + sound * addition factor + parameter_value * multiplication_factor * sound ;
where:
sound - effect of average amplitude or pitch of the selected range of sound frequencies. It is calculated as a value from 0 to 1, ( 0 = silent , 1 = maximum.)
parameter value - from keyframe animation calculations.
animation - value of the parameter value after the sound has been applied.
To get subtraction of the sound value from parameter value, use Negative influence option.
animsound_pitchmode:
Changes the way the sound is calculated.
If the mode is disabled, then the sound is calculated from the average amplitude of the selected sound frequencies.
When it is enabled, then the sound is calculated from the average pitch of the selected sound frequencies.
animsound_midfreq:
Frequency of sound which will be used to calculate animation.
This frequency is shown on the "Frequency spectrum" chart.
animsound_bandwidth:
Width of the band of frequencies used to calculate the sound value effect on an animation.
Selected bandwidth is shown on the "Frequency spectrum" chart.
If the bandwidth is wide, then the sound value will be calculated from the average amplitude of the selected frequencies.
If the bandwidth is set to the maximum value, then the sound value will be calculated from the amplitude of the sound.
animsound_multfactor:
The value of animation of a parameter, is the sum of the sound value added to the parameter value (from the keyframe animation table):
animation = parameter_value + parameter_value * multiplication_factor * sound + sound * addition factor ;
where:
sound - average amplitude or pitch of the selected range of sound frequencies. It is calculated as a value from 0 to 1, ( 0 = silent , 1 = maximum.)
parameter value - from keyframe animation calculations.
animation - value of the parameter value after the sound_value has been added.
Note: when only multiplication factor is used (i.e. addition_factor is close to zero), it is guaranteed that sound will not modify the sign of animated parameter value.
Note: multiplication_factor operates differently in Negative Influence mode function. There it is used as division instead of multiplication. Negative Influence mode function:
animation = parameter_value / (1.0 + multiplication_factor * sound) + sound * addition factor;
animsound_binaryfilter:
This option enables the binary filter.
The addition of the sound value to the parameter value is triggered when the sound rises above the threshold and ceases when the sound drops below the threshold, (unless the minimum duration is extended past that frame point.)
animsound_binarylength: Minimum duration for which the sound value will be calculated and added to the parameter value, from the frame where the sound first exceeded the threshold, ( measured in frames.)
animsound_binarythresh:
Threshold for binary filter.
When sound is above the threshold, the sound value is calculated and added to the parameter value. Calculation continues until the sound falls below the threshold or the minimum duration is exceeded.
animsound_decayfilter:
This option enables the decay filter.
The sound value will rise fast, but decay slowly.
animsound_decaystrength: A higher value extends the decay of the sound value.
animsound_smoothfilter:
This option enables the smooth filter.
The sound value will change in a smooth way.
animsound_smoothstrength: A higher value will result in a reduced audio influence on the animated parameter.

flight_animation:
In record flight mode, the camera is operated like in a flight simulator game. Flight path is recorded. It recommended to use low image resolution for better recording performance.
Render animation button starts rendering of the recorded flight path. For final rendering you can select higher image resolution.
To add a parameter, right click on the selected parameter's edit field and select from context menu Add to flight animation
You can modify frame parameters directly in the animation table or by editing parameters in fractal or effects edit fields (double click keyframe preview or right click on a keyframe, and choose Render this keyframe , this updates parameters in window, then modify parameters and click Modify keyframe to get modified parameters into table)
You can click on Export to keyframes to continue editing animation in Keyframe animation editor
Animation is stored in a settings file in CSV format, therefore it is possible to edit animation with external tools (e.g spreadsheet editor or text editor).
render_flight: Starts rendering of previously recorded flight path
record_flight:
Starts recording flight path.
It is recommended to decrease image resolution for better rendering performance.
The mouse pointer is used as the controller.
Move the mouse pointer to change flight direction.
Left mouse button increases flight speed. Right mouse button decreases speed.
Arrow keys moves camera up, down, left and right (move sidewards)
Z and X keys rotate the camera (roll)
Spacebar pauses flight path recording .

keyframe_animation:
This feature is for rendering animations by interpolating between keyframes.
You can create multiple keyframes, each with different parameters (i.e.camera, fractal and environment parameters values). Intermediate frames will be calculated during rendering of the animation.
To add a keyframe to the animation table, click Add keyframe .
To add a parameter, right click on the selected parameter's edit field and select from context menu Add to keyframe animation
Build an animation by adding, inserting and deleting keyframes. Modify parameters directly in the animation table, or in fractal or effects edit fields (double click keyframe preview or right click on a keyframe, and choose Render this keyframe , this updates parameters in window, then modify parameters and click Modify keyframe to refresh animation table.)
Each parameter can have assigned different type of interpolation (right click on animation parameter name.)
Animation is stored in a settings file in CSV format, therefore it is possible to edit animation with external tools (e.g spreadsheet editor or text editor).
Animation can be exported to Flight Animation, where it is possible to edit each frame.

effects:
Flip the direction of Chromatic Aberration (RGB channel offset).
When enabled, the color fringing shifts in the opposite radial direction: - Off: channels shift outward from the image center. - On: channels shift inward toward the center. This also swaps the apparent order of the colored fringes.
raytraced_reflections:
Activate calculation of ray-traced reflections and transparency. Reflectance can be set by Material/Reflection. Transparency settings are in the same tab as reflection.
Also enable with Monte Carlo global illumination.
reflections_max:
Maximum number of ray bounces which are calculated for a given pixel.
This value affects reflections, refraction and MC Global Illumination
DOF_enabled:
Depth of field is the effect in which objects within some range of distances in a scene appear in focus, and objects nearer or farther than this range appear out of focus.
note: using DOF prevents one-pass anaglyph rendering, unless Monte carlo algorithm mode is selected.
DOF_focus:
It's the distance where objects appear in focus.
Distance can be set bu using button Set focus distance by mouse

low focus distance
high focus distance
DOF_radius:
Intensity of DOF effect (average radius of blur)

radius = 10
radius = 50
DOF_number_of_passes: Number of passes of rendering DOF effect. One pass is enough for most of cases. But for more realistic blur it can be increased (e.g to 4) and blur opacity should be accordingly decreased (e.g. to 1.0)
DOF_blur_opacity: Opacity of blur effect used during second phase of rendering the DOF effect. 4.0 is correct for most of cases. But for more realistic blur the number of passes can be increased (e.g to 4) and blur opacity should be accordingly decreased (e.g. to 1.0)
DOF_max_radius: Maximum radius of generated blur. Lower value can speed up rendering but effect will be less realistic.
DOF_update: Update image after changes of DOF settings. Can be updated even after image rendering.
DOF_set_focus:
Setting of focus distance by mouse pointer.
Click on this button and then point the object on image which you want to appear in focus.
After using it don't forget to change Navigation / Mouse click function to continue work with the camera.
DOF_monte_carlo:
Enables Monte Carlo algorithms for rendering the depth of field (DOF), global illumination, ambient occlusion (with multiple rays) and soft shadows effects. This mode is extremely slow for rendering, but gives a very realistic appearance of effects.
In addition Monte Carlo algorithm provides high quality adaptive anti-aliasing.
Every pixed (or tile) of the image is rendered multiple times with randomly changed parameters. Every repeat reduces noise. Sampling of each pixel (or tile) is stopped when noise is reduced to defined level (defined by "Max noise level" parameter") or when maximum number of repeats is reached (defined by "Max number of samples").
Remark: This effect cannot work properly when screen space ambient occlusion is enabled.
average_DOF_samples: Average number of MC samples that have been calculated for each image pixel.
DOF_max_noise:
Limit of noise level for each image pixel. Every pixel is calculated multiple times until estimated noise reaches maximum noise level percentage.
A lower value reduces visible noise on the final image, but increases rendering time. Decreasing the maximum noise level by half, increases the rendering time by 4.
average_DOF_noise: Estimated average noise caused by Monte Carlo effects.
DOF_min_samples: Minimum number of MC samples calculated for each image pixel. Increasing this parameter can reduce visible noise, ( by improving calculation of noise level estimation).
DOF_samples:
Number of MC samples calculated for each image pixel. Higher values reduce the noise on the image but increase the rendering time.
For instance if the number of samples is 100, then the rendering will take 100 times longer compared to the effect disabled.
masked_pixels: Estimated average noise caused by Monte Carlo effects.
tiles_done: Estimated average noise caused by Monte Carlo effects.
MC_pixel_level_optimization:
Enables additonal optimization of MC rendering. The noise level is calculated separatelly for each pixel. If noise level is enough low, then the pixel is no longer calculated.
If the image is very noisy and there is low value of Min number of samples , then enabling this option can cause dark random pixels left on the image.
MC_denoiser_enable: Enable the Monte Carlo denoiser to reduce noise in rendered images. This post-processing step smooths out grainy patterns caused by limited sampling, resulting in cleaner and more visually appealing results, especially at lower sample counts.
MC_denoiser_strength:
Sets the strength of the Monte Carlo denoiser for noise reduction in rendered images:
Light: Minimal denoising with the smallest blur radius. Preserves the most detail but leaves some noise.
Medium: Balanced setting with moderate blur. Reduces noise while retaining most image details.
Strong: Aggressive denoising with a larger blur radius. Produces smoother images but may blur fine details.
Extreme: Maximum denoising with the largest blur. Greatly reduces noise but can noticeably smooth out textures and edges.
Choose a strength based on your preference for image smoothness versus detail preservation.
MC_denoiser_preserve_geometry:
Preserve geometry and edges during denoising.
When enabled, the denoiser uses depth and surface normal information to keep object boundaries and fine details sharp, reducing unwanted blurring of shapes.
Note: In scenes with strong depth of field (DOF), enabling this option may lead to unnatural appearance near blurred edges.
DOF_MC_global_illumination:
Enables calculation of realistic global illumination using Monte Carlo algorithm.
Number of light bounces is defined by the "reflections depth" parameter at the top of tab.
MC_GI_radiance_limit: Limit for intensity of bounced light. Lower value reduces noise caused by very bright spots on HDR background textures.
MC_global_illumination_volumetric:
Enable global illumination for volumetric effects such as fog and clouds.
When checked, indirect lighting will account for light scattering inside volumes, resulting in more realistic illumination for scenes with participating media.
This may increase rendering time.
MC_fog_illumination:
Enable global illumination for volumetric fog.
When checked, indirect lighting (from global illumination) will contribute to the brightness and realism of fog and other volumetric effects, allowing light to scatter and bounce inside fog.
This results in more realistic lighting but may increase render time.
MC_soft_shadows_enable:
Enables calculation of realistic soft shadows using Monte Carlo algorithm.
Soft shadow cone for main light source is defined by Soft shadow code angle ( Lights tab)
Soft shadow cone for auxiliary lights is defined by C ustom lights options / Size.
DOF_MC_CA_enable:
Enables rendering of chromatic aberration. This effect simulates the way an actual lens refracts light slightly differently based on wavelength.
It will give a "rainbow" type effect that gets stronger closer to the edges of the image.
DOF_MC_CA_dispersion_gain: Higher value makes dispersion of refracted light more vsible on transparent objects.
DOF_MC_CA_camera_dispersion: Higher value makes simulated dispersion of camera lenses more visible.

clouds_enable: Enable procedural volumetric clouds. When checked, the renderer integrates noise-based cloud volumes along view rays, with per-light illumination and optional shadow casting/receiving (if enabled in Clouds settings). Configure color, density, scale (period), noise iterations, height/plane shape, distance mode, and motion below. Increases render time due to volumetric sampling and shadow queries.
clouds_noise_iterations:
Number of noise octaves used to generate cloud density.
Higher values add finer, more turbulent detail and richer structure, but increase computation time due to additional noise sampling. Typical useful range: 5–12. Adjust together with Cloud Period and Detail Accuracy; higher iterations with a small period produce very high-frequency features.
clouds_density:
Base density/coverage of the volumetric cloud field (0–1). Higher values produce thicker, more continuous clouds; lower values yield sparse, broken clouds.
Tune together with Cloud Opacity (overall strength), Period (scale), and Noise Iterations (detail). Typical range: 0.15–0.60; 0 = clear, 1 = near-solid overcast.
clouds_period:
Spatial scale of the procedural cloud noise (period, in scene units). Larger values yield bigger, smoother cloud structures; smaller values create finer, more turbulent detail.
Interacts with Noise Iterations and Detail Accuracy; very small periods may increase render time and require higher Detail Accuracy to avoid aliasing.
clouds_random_seed: Random seed for the procedural noise field driving clouds. Changing it generates a different (statistically equivalent) cloud layout/phase without altering density, scale (period), or octave structure. Keep constant for deterministic, reproducible renders and animations; vary to explore alternative compositions. Integer value, typically 0–1,000,000.
clouds_ambient_light:
Ambient light contribution for clouds (0–1).
Blends uniform ambient illumination into cloud lighting:
0 = only direct lights with full shadow contrast;
1 = fully ambient, very soft/flat shadows.
Increase to brighten interiors and soften shadows; decrease for crisper shading.
Does not affect opacity.
Typical range: 0.05–0.30.
clouds_lights_boost:
Boosts intensity of visible light beams and orbit‑trap “fake lights” inside clouds. Scales their contribution with cloud density/opacity: higher values make light shafts brighter and more pronounced, especially in dense regions.
Does not affect direct/ambient light or cloud opacity.
0 = no boost. Typical range 0–2; use higher for strong god‑ray effects (may increase noise).
clouds_randomize:
Generates a new random seed for the procedural cloud noise, changing the cloud pattern without altering density, period, or noise iterations.
Click repeatedly to explore variations; keep the chosen seed fixed for reproducible renders and animations.
clouds_opacity: Global multiplier for volumetric cloud opacity (thickness). Higher values make clouds denser and more opaque; lower values make them more transparent (0 = invisible). Works together with Cloud Density, Noise Iterations, and Sharp Edges. Accepts positive real values; typical range 10–1000 depending on scene. Has minimal impact on render time.
clouds_cast_shadows: Enable cloud shadowing. When checked, clouds receive and cast shadows from scene lights, giving more realistic occlusion and higher contrast; this is slower. When unchecked, faster shading without shadows. Tip: raise Clouds Ambient Light to soften shadows; use Lights Boost to emphasize light shafts.
clouds_sharp_edges:
Enable hard‑edged clouds by sharpening the density threshold. When on, use Sharpness to control edge steepness: higher values produce crisper, thinner transitions; lower values keep edges softer.
Great for dramatic silhouettes and pronounced shadows.
May increase noise/aliasing—raise Clouds Noise Iterations or Detail Accuracy if needed.
clouds_sharpness:
Edge steepness for Sharp edges clouds. Higher values sharpen the density threshold (crisper, thinner cloud contours); lower values keep transitions soft.
Very high values may introduce aliasing/noise—consider increasing Clouds Noise Iterations or Clouds Detail Accuracy.
clouds_speed_x:
X-axis drift speed of the clouds. Controls how fast the noise field moves along +X over time (animation).
Positive = moves toward +X, negative = toward −X; 0 = no motion.
Effective speed scales with Clouds Period.
Use small values (e.g., ±0.001 to ±0.05).
Combine with Y/Z for wind direction.
clouds_primitive: Selects the geometric primitive used to define the spatial boundaries of basic fog. The chosen shape (such as box, sphere, or other available primitives) determines where in the scene the basic fog effect will be applied, allowing for precise control over the fog’s location and extent.
clouds_plane_shape:
Enable planar cloud layer. Constrains clouds to a band around a rotated plane with a soft vertical falloff.
Use Height to set layer thickness, and Center/Rotation to position and tilt the layer.
Useful for horizon-like cloud sheets and can speed up rendering by limiting the cloud volume.

clouds_center_x: Vertical position (X axis) of the center of the clouds volume relative to the fractal.

clouds_DE_approaching: Step size for distance estimation when approaching the clouds; lower values increase accuracy but reduce performance.
clouds_detail_accuracy: Controls the rendering accuracy for fine details in the clouds; higher values improve detail but increase render time.
clouds_DE_multiplier: Multiplier for the distance estimation step size in clouds rendering. Increasing this value can speed up rendering but may reduce accuracy and detail in cloud boundaries. Lower values provide more precise results at the cost of performance.

all_lights_intensity:
Global intensity multiplier for all lights (Light #1…#N). Multiplies each light’s Intensity value: 1.0 = no change, 0 = lights off, >1 brightens, <1 dims.
Useful for balancing overall lighting without editing each light.
all_lights_size:
Global size multiplier for all lights’ visible glow/halo. Multiplies each light’s Size value: 1.0 = no change; >1 enlarges halos, <1 shrinks them.
Also scales the apparent angular size for directional lights.
rayleigh_scattering_blue:
Strength of blue Rayleigh scattering for volumetric effects (atmosphere).
Higher values add a blue, angle‑dependent tint around lights (∝ 1 + cos²θ). Set to 0 to disable.
Use with Rayleigh scattering red to balance the effect.
all_lights_visibility:
Global multiplier for all lights’ Visibility (the visible glow/illuminated fog around lights).
Multiplies each light’s Visibility value: 1.0 = no change, 0 = hide visible lights, >1 increases glow.
rayleigh_scattering_red:
Strength of red Mie scattering for volumetric effects (atmosphere). Increases warm, forward‑scattering glow when looking toward the light direction (stronger near beams/god‑rays).
1.0 = noticeable effect; 0 = off.
Use together with Rayleigh scattering blue to balance overall color.
aux_light_manual_placement_dist:
Controls distance from the fractal surface where the light will be placed with mouse pointer. When it's zero, the light will be set on fractal surface. A higher value moves the light towards the camera.
This parameter can be controlled with mouse wheel + alt key.
aux_light_place_behind:
When placing a light with the mouse, position it behind the clicked surface (traced through the fractal). When disabled, the light is placed in front of the surface at the manual placement distance.
Use to hide the emitter behind geometry while keeping its illumination/visible glow. Applies to the “Place light” mouse action.
random_lights_group:
Random seed: random seed for lights distribution
Maximum distance from the fractal: random lights are placed within this distance from the fractal surface
Centre of distribution X, Y, Z: the centre point for random light distribution. To set this point by mouse pointer, select "Set position of centre for random lights" in Mouse click function combo box in Mandelbulber Render Window
Distribution radius of lights: maximum distance from Centre of distribution where lights can be placed. The random lights appear in the region that matches the condition of being both within this radius and also within the maximum distance from fractal surface.
If this radius is too small to generate random lights, then the program will automatically increase this radius.
random_lights_intensity:
Per‑light brightness for auto‑generated random lights.
Does not depend on “Number of random lights” — adding more lights does not auto‑scale intensity. Increase for brighter illumination; very high values can cause overexposure. Adjust together with Visibility and Size for desired look.
random_lights_max_distance_from_fractal:
Maximum distance from the fractal surface used when placing auto-generated random lights. Only positions within this distance from the surface are accepted.
Lower values keep lights close to the surface; higher values allow them to float farther out. Very small values may slow placement or yield few/no lights.
random_lights_distribution_center_y:
Center point (X/Y/Z) for placing auto-generated random lights. Lights are distributed around this point within the Distribution radius.
Use “Place random light center” to pick it with the mouse. Works together with “Maximum distance from fractal” to keep lights near the surface.
random_lights_coloring_type:
Choose how auto‑generated random lights are colored.
Random colors — each light gets a random color.
Single color — all lights use the First color.
Two colors — each light randomly uses the First or Second color.
Two colors based on distance — color blends between First and Second color based on the light’s distance to the fractal surface (closer → First, farther → Second).
random_lights_number:
Number of auto-generated random lights.
Lights are placed around the Center of distribution within the Distribution radius, constrained by Maximum distance from fractal, and initialized using the Random seed.
Higher values may slow rendering and clutter the scene.
random_lights_random_seed:
Random seed for generating auto-created lights. With the same seed and settings, the random lights’ positions/colors are reproducible; change it to get a different arrangement.
Integer 0–999999. Does not change the number of lights, only their randomized outcome.
random_lights_cast_shadows:
Enable shadow casting for auto‑generated random lights.
When on, these lights occlude geometry and produce shadows. Turn off to use them as non‑shadowing fill lights and speed up rendering. For soft, blurry shadows, also enable “Calculate MC soft shadows” and adjust “Soft shadow cone”. Otherwise shadows are hard.
place_random_lights_by_mouse:
Pick the center for auto-generated random lights by clicking in the image.
Sets the mouse mode to “Place random light center”. On click, it also auto-sets Distribution radius to 50% and Maximum distance from fractal to 10% of the distance from the chosen center to the camera.
random_lights_distribution_radius:
Radius of the area around the Center of distribution where auto-generated random lights are placed (±radius along X/Y/Z).
Increase to spread lights wider; decrease to cluster them near the center. Works with “Maximum distance from fractal” to keep lights near the surface.
random_lights_distribution_center_x:
Center point (X/Y/Z) for placing auto-generated random lights. Lights are distributed around this point within the Distribution radius.
Use “Place random light center” to pick it with the mouse. Works together with “Maximum distance from fractal” to keep lights near the surface.
random_lights_distribution_center_z:
Center point (X/Y/Z) for placing auto-generated random lights. Lights are distributed around this point within the Distribution radius.
Use “Place random light center” to pick it with the mouse. Works together with “Maximum distance from fractal” to keep lights near the surface.
random_lights_soft_shadow_cone:
Soft shadow cone angle for auto‑generated random lights (degrees).
Sets the angular radius used by Monte Carlo soft‑shadow sampling. 0 = hard, crisp shadows; higher values produce softer, blurrier shadows.
Effective when “Cast shadows” is on, and “Calculate MC soft shadows” is enabled.
random_lights_penetrating:
Allow auto‑generated random lights to penetrate geometry.
When enabled, these lights are partally blocked by objects and can illuminate through walls or inside cavities—useful as fill lights. For realistic, blocked lighting and shadows, turn this off.
random_lights_size:
Emitter size (radius) of each auto‑generated random light.
Larger values behave more like area lights, producing softer shadows and broader highlights; smaller values approach point lights with sharper shadows. Very large sizes can flatten contrast.
Effective when “Random lights group” is enabled. Default: 0.1.
random_lights_visibility:
Brightness of the visible light source (glow/halo) for each auto‑generated random light.
Affects only how strongly the emitter itself is drawn on screen; it does not change scene illumination (use “Intensity” for that). Works together with “Size” to define the halo’s radius. Not used for directional lights.
Higher values make brighter, more noticeable bulbs.
fake_lights_enabled:
Simulates a large amount of lights and is relatively fast to render.
An orbit trap is a point, a 2D, or 3D shape defined in 3D space. The brightness of the point is dependent on how close the point's orbit gets to the orbit trap shape during the chosen iterations.
This effect is difficult to setup and often you need to try many different orbit trap settings.
These light sources illuminate the fractal surface, but do not cast shadows.
Example:
fake_lights_relative_center:
Interpret the Orbit trap center relative to the fractal’s origin.
When enabled, the orbit‑trap distance is computed using coordinates relative to the fractal start/constant (z − C), effectively anchoring the trap to the fractal’s local origin. When disabled, the distance uses absolute coordinates (z), so the trap center is in world space.
fake_lights_orbit_trap_size:
Size of the Orbit trap shape used by Fake lights.
Meaning depends on Shape: - Circle: ring radius - Square: half edge length - Sphere: shell radius - Cube: half edge length - Point/Line: this value is not used
Applied in the trap’s local space around the Orbit trap center. Use “Thickness” to control the shell’s falloff width.
fake_lights_min_iter: First iteration taken for orbit trap calculation
fake_lights_orbit_trap_shape:
Select the orbit‑trap shape used by Fake lights (lighting is driven by the distance to this shape).
Point — a single point source near the trap center (default).
Line — an infinite line through the center; use Orbit rotation to set its direction.
Circle — a circular ring around a central axis; Size = ring radius; Rotation sets the axis.
Square — a square ring; Size = half edge; Rotation sets orientation.
Sphere — a spherical shell; Size = radius.
Cube — a cubic shell; Size = half edge length.
Tip: Use Thickness to control falloff width, Visibility/Visibility size for reach, and set center/Relative center and Orbit rotation as needed. Effective when “Fake lights” is enabled.
fake_lights_visibility:
Brightness of visible lights. It is volumetric effect.
Quality of this effect can by controled by Effects / Volumetric / Custom DE step multiplier for volumetric effects
fake_lights_orbit_rotation_z:
Rotate the Orbit trap shape around the selected axis (degrees).
Effects by shape: - Line: sets the line direction. - Circle: sets the ring’s axis. - Square: sets the plane/orientation. - Cube: sets the cube orientation. - Sphere: usually no visible effect. - Point: no effect.
Notes: - Angles are in degrees; internal order is Z → Y → X. - Rotation is applied around the Orbit trap center (see “Relative center”).
fake_lights_orbit_rotation_x:
Rotate the Orbit trap shape around the selected axis (degrees).
Effects by shape: - Line: sets the line direction. - Circle: sets the ring’s axis. - Square: sets the plane/orientation. - Cube: sets the cube orientation. - Sphere: usually no visible effect. - Point: no effect.
Notes: - Angles are in degrees; internal order is Z → Y → X. - Rotation is applied around the Orbit trap center (see “Relative center”).
fake_lights_orbit_rotation_y:
Rotate the Orbit trap shape around the selected axis (degrees).
Effects by shape: - Line: sets the line direction. - Circle: sets the ring’s axis. - Square: sets the plane/orientation. - Cube: sets the cube orientation. - Sphere: usually no visible effect. - Point: no effect.
Notes: - Angles are in degrees; internal order is Z → Y → X. - Rotation is applied around the Orbit trap center (see “Relative center”).
fake_lights_intensity: Intensity of illumination of fractal surface
fake_lights_max_iter: Last iteration taken for orbit trap calculation
fake_lights_visibility_size: Size of visible lights (scale is logarithmic)
post_effects_update: Update image after changes of DOF settings. Can be updated even after image rendering.
hdr_blur_enabled:
Enable the HDR Blur post effect (bloom-like glow on bright areas).
This applies a weighted blur in HDR space after rendering. Controls below: - Radius: overall spread of the blur (image-size relative). - Intensity: strength/threshold of the blur contribution.
Notes: - Operates on HDR image data; does not change lighting or exposure. - Uses OpenCL if available, otherwise CPU. - Larger Radius increases render time.
hdr_blur_radius:
Sets the radius (spread) of the HDR Blur bloom.
The blur size is relative to image dimensions. Approximate pixel radius = radius × (image width + image height) × 0.001.
Larger values give a wider, softer glow; smaller values keep highlights tight. Bigger radius increases processing time. Works with Intensity to control strength.
hdr_blur_intensity:
Copilot said:
Controls the strength/threshold of the HDR Blur
Controls the strength/threshold of the HDR Blur contribution.
Lower values produce a stronger, brighter bloom; higher values dampen the effect. Works together with Radius (spread) but does not change blur size.
post_chromatic_aberration_enabled:
Enable the Chromatic Aberration post effect (RGB channel separation).
This simulates lens dispersion by shifting color channels radially from the image center.
Controls inside: - Radius: overall spread of the separation (relative to image size). - Aberration intensity: strength of the channel offset. - Reverse: flip direction (outward vs inward shift).
Notes: - Post-processing only; does not affect lighting or geometry. - Uses OpenCL if available.
post_chromatic_aberration_intensity:
Controls the strength of RGB channel separation (color fringing) in Chromatic Aberration.
Higher values increase the offset between color channels and widen the visible fringes, especially toward the image edges. Lower values keep the effect subtle. Works together with Radius (spread) and does not change direction (use Reverse to flip).
Notes: - Stronger intensity can increase processing time. - Post-processing only; does not affect lighting or geometry.
post_chromatic_aberration_radius:
Sets the base radius (spread) of Chromatic Aberration.
The effective spread is relative to image size and grows with distance from the image center, producing wider color fringing toward the edges. Increase for more pronounced, wider separation; decrease to keep fringes tight.
Notes: - Works with Aberration intensity (strength); does not change direction (see Reverse). - Larger values increase processing time.
image_width: Width of rendered image in pixel
image_height: Height of rendered image in pixel
antialiasing_enabled:
Enable anti-aliasing (supersampling) to reduce jagged edges and shimmering.
How it works: - Renders multiple subpixel samples per pixel and averages them. - “Number of samples (n × n)” sets the subpixel grid; total samples per pixel = n² (e.g., 2 × 2 = 4 samples).
Notes: - Improves edge smoothness and animation stability (less flicker). - Increases render time approximately proportional to n². - Uncheck to disable anti-aliasing entirely.
antialiasing_size:
Set the anti-aliasing sample grid size (n).
Each pixel is sampled on an n × n subpixel grid and averaged; total samples per pixel = n².
Notes: - 1 = no supersampling (fastest). - Higher n reduces jagged edges and shimmering but increases render time roughly by n². - Takes effect only when Anti-aliasing is enabled.
antialiasing_ocl_depth:
Select the total number of OpenCL anti-aliasing samples per pixel.
Use in OpenCL anti-aliasing mode only. Higher values reduce jaggies and shimmering but increase render time roughly proportionally.
Options (samples/pixel): 5, 9, 45, 81, 405, 729.
Notes: - Effective only when OpenCL AA is enabled; the regular “n × n” grid is ignored in this mode. - With “Adaptive (faster)” enabled, fewer samples may be used in low-detail areas.
antialiasing_adaptive:
Adaptive anti-aliasing (OpenCL): vary samples per pixel based on image detail to speed up rendering.
Behavior: - Uses fewer samples in flat/low-contrast areas; uses up to the selected maximum near edges and fine detail. - Usually faster with minimal quality loss, but may increase noise or flicker in animations.
Notes: - Effective only in OpenCL anti-aliasing mode; ignored in regular n × n CPU AA. - “Number of samples (OpenCL mode)” sets the maximum samples per pixel.
connect_detail_level:
When this option is enabled, the fractal appearance is maintained at all resolutions.
The fractal detail level will be automatically adjusted to match any change of image resolution.
For instance, if the resolution is doubled then the detail level will be reduced by half.
stereo_enabled: Enables rendering of stereoscopic images and animations for viewing with 3D glasses.
stereo_mode:
Defines how stereoscopic image will be rendered.
Left-right - View for left eye will be rendered on the left side of the image. View for right eye will be on the right side.
Top-bottom - View for left eye will be rendered on the top half of the image. View for right eye will be on the bottom half of the image.
Anaglyph red/cyan - Image will be rendered as an anaglyph dedicated for red/cyan 3D glasses. Using this option it is possible to edit the fractal with 3D view directly in the application window using regular display. Cheap 3D glasses are all that is required. For fractal exploration it is recommended to not use SSAO ambient occlusion, because it is rendered in 2 passes (try to use "Fast" ambient occlusion).
stereo_swap_eyes: Swaps left and right eye on rendered image.
stereo_eye_distance:
The distance between two virtual eyes. Higher values make the 3D effect more intense.
The optimal distance between eyes is about 1%-5% of the distance to the viewed object.
stereo_infinite_correction:
Adjusts the appearance of the 3D effect for the furthest objects (or background). If the value of this parameter is higher then the background objects will appear further away.
As an example, the optimal value of this parameter for a 24 inch display could be about 0.4. For bigger display this value should be lower.
quality_preset_normal:
Normal quality preset.
Ambient occlusion is turned on in Screen Space Ambient Occlusion (SSAO) mode.
quality_preset_low:
A fast preset but with low quality.
Ambient occlusion is turned off.
quality_preset_high:
The highest quality preset and the slowest.
Ambient occlusion is turned on in Multiple Rays mode. Raymarching step is decreased to 0.2 to reduce fractal calculation errors.
quality_preset_very_low:
This is the fastest preset but with the lowest quality.
Shadows, ambient occlusion and raytraced reflections are turned off. Detail level is decreased to 0.5.

Open a new Navigator window initialized with the current scene and camera for interactive navigation and view selection.

temporary_scale:
Temporarily downscale rendering resolution for faster previews.
Options: - 1 = full resolution (no downscale). - 1/2, 1/4, … 1/64 = render with width and height divided by 2, 4, … 64 (roughly N² speedup).
Notes: - Affects only temporary/preview renders; image_width/height and saved outputs are unchanged. - Useful during navigation and Auto refresh; set back to 1 for final quality renders.
opencl_mode:
Modes for OpenCL computation (GPU support):
no OpenCL - use only CPU
fast - very fast rendering on GPU. Fractal has visible shape, but colors and effects are not calculated. It is very good mode for fast camera navigation and looking for interesting fractal shapes in auto-refresh mode.
medium - medium rendering speed on GPU. There is calculated color of the fractal, light sources with shadows are used. There is used only first defined material. Reflections and volumetric effects are not calculated.
full - the most accurate and the the slowest rendering. Uses more GPU resources. All effects are calculated .
auto_refresh:
Automatically re-render the image when any setting changes.
Behavior: - Checks for changes at a fixed interval and starts a new render only if parameters changed.
Tips: - The interval is set in Preferences → Image auto-refresh period. - For faster previews, combine with Temporary scale (e.g., 1/4, 1/8); set back to 1 for final renders. - May increase CPU/GPU usage; turn off for manual control.

bailout:
The vector values are checked during each iteration of fractal formula to see if they have reached a critical 'escape' condition or 'bailout'. If that condition is reached, the calculation is stopped. Condition is: if length of vector is greater than bailout, then break iteration loop.
In some cases higher value can increase image quality, but it will increase rendering time.
use_default_bailout: Enables using default (recommended) bailout value. Each fractal formula has different optimal bailout value.
N:
The higher the maximum number of iterations ("maxiter") is, the more detail and subtlety emerge in the final image, but also the longer time it will take to calculate the fractal image.
In normal operation this should be set as high as possible because "Distance estimation" algorithm limits number of iteration (almost no influence on rendering speed)
When Stop at maximum iteration is selected, then this parameter controls detail level.

maxiter = 10
maxiter = 15
optimization_MQ:
Optimize 'Raymarching step multiplier' for medium image quality.
It gives 0.1% of wrong distance estimations (pixels with potential noise)
delta_DE_method:
Distance estimation is a method which calculates approximate distance to fractal surface from any point in space.
- Automatic mode uses distance estimation method defined for selected fractal
- Force "Delta DE" method uses Delta DE algorithm which is slower but works also with untypical fractal configurations
DE_factor:
This parameter has the biggest influence on overall quality of image and rendering speed.
Higher value gives faster rendering but more noise on image.
When rays are traced, for each step there are estimated distances to the fractal surface. Optimally , the jump distance for every ray-marching step would be equal to the estimated distance. This would produce a small number of steps and good quality. However the distance can be only estimated, so it's not always accurate. It can produce oversteppings which will be visible on the image as random noise.
In some cases you need to adjust this parameter to find a balance between acceptable image quality and a reasonable rendering time.

step multiplier = 1.0 (optimal - good quality and fast)
step multiplier = 5 (visible strong noise on image)

As a quality indicator, the Percentage of wrong distance estimations ( visible in Statistics dock ) can be used .
To optimize this parameter the histograms of iteration count and ray-marching step count, can be used .
wrong_DE_percentage:
Percentage of points on image which are probably calculated wrong.
Higher value usually means more visible noise or artifacts on image.
optimization_LQ:
Optimize 'Raymarching step multiplier' for low image quality and fast rendering
It gives 1% of wrong distance estimations (pixels with potential noise)
delta_DE_function:
Distance estimation function is specific to the fractal formula calculations.
In some fractal fomulas the length of the iteration vector increases exponentially and some in a linear manner.
- Automatic mode - finds the probable best function based on the fractal formulas used.
- Logarithmic - the best for fractals with exponential growth of iteration vector (e.g. Mandelbulb)
- Linear - the best for fractals with linear growth of iteration vector (e.g. Mandelbox, IFS)
- Pseudo Kleinian - linear growth distance estimation function for working with Pseudo Kleinian formulas
- JosKleinian - linear growth distance estimation function for working with JosKleinian formulas
- Custom - distance estimation function where the distance estimation out.distance is calculated entirely in the formula.
optimization_HQ:
Optimize 'Raymarching step multiplier' for high image quality and slow rendering
It gives 0.01% of wrong distance estimations (pixels with potential noise)

Higher value gives more detailed image, but slows down rendering.

advanced_quality: Access advanced quality settings for fine-tuning raymarching steps, detail size, and rendering precision.
rel_max_marching_step:
Maximum relative step for raymarching. It is related to local detail size. Close to the camera, the limit is lower (visible details are smaller).
Lower value can improve calculation accuracy far from the fractal surface.
detail_size_min: Higher value can produce less detail in areas close to the camera.
rel_min_marching_step:
Minimum relative step for raymarching. It is related to local detail size. Close to the camera, the limit is lower (visible details are smaller).
Higher value can speed up calculation of raymarching in areas close to the fractal surface.
deltade_relative_delta: Controls delta used in DeltaDE distance algorithm. Tuning of this parameter can improve quality when there is noise caused by inaccurate distance estimation.

netrender:
This feature allows the connection of multiple computers into a network to share rendering.
The same image or animation can be rendered using an unlimited number of computers. The increased computing power will reduce rendering time.
netrender_mode:
Switches between server and client.
Server is the main application in the network. It controls rendering process, sends data to all clients and collects data from them.
Server compiles parts of images received from the clients and finally displays the whole image. It also renders image.
Client receives jobs from server. It renders only the parts of the image which the server ask for. It displays only partial image.
To start rendering process on all computers you need to press Render button on Server.
netrender_client_remote_address: IP address or name of the computer where Mandelbulber is launched in server mode.
netrender_client_remote_port: Port number which is set on Mandelbulber which runs in server mode.

Establish connection with server.
When connection is established, status should change to READY
netrender_server_local_port: Internet port number which will be used for server. This port has to not be blocked by a firewall or passed through a router.
netrender_start_server:
Starts Mandelbulber to work as server.
After pressing this button, application starts to watch clients and connect to them.
If connection with a client is established, then this client is displayed in the table below.
To establish a connection with a client, the Connect button must be pressed on the client side
If all needed computers are already connected, then the server is ready for operation. If you press Render button, then the server and all the clients will start rendering of the same image.

No action - blocks functionality of mouse pointer Move the camera - moves the camera or target (depends on movement and rotation mode) Set fog visibility - sets visibility distance for basic fog effect Set DOF focus - sets object which will appear in focus Get Julia constant - gets value of constant for Julia fractal Place light #n - places light in selected place (mouse wheel controls distance from fractal)
multiMode: Auto - Rotation mode depends on used button
without_camera: Closes the Navigator and copies actual parameters to the main window. It does not copy camera position and rotation.
auto_refresh_period: Multiplies fractal c constant by this value.
opencl_job_size_multiplier:
Job size multiplier increases size of OpenCL jobs (size of tiles).
Higher value can increase rendering speed, but too high can slow down rendering.
Too high value can cause higher GPU memory usage makeing the program unstable. It also increases the time of rendering a single tile, which can cause GPU driver timeouts.
opencl_disable_build_cache: It disables 'compute cache' used by NVidia driver. It is sometimes needed to use this option to refresh precompiled OpenCL programs after changing OpenCL source files (e.g. after upgrade of the program).
opencl_use_fast_relaxed_math:
It enables -cl-fast-relaxed-math OpenCL flag. It provides additional speed by removing some checks to the math operations like division by zero or Not-a-Number. In some cases it can lead to unpredictable results.
It is needed to restart the program to apply this option.
opencl_memory_limit:
Memory limit for single memory buffer used by OpenCL programs.
It should be set not higher than suggested memory limit showed below.
If SSAO or DOF effects need more memory than limit, they will be rendered using CPU.
Higher memory limit can allow rendering SSAO and DOF effects using GPU at higher resolution, but program can produce errors or be unstable.
placePrimitive:
Place a light source using the mouse pointer.
Light position (for selected light tab) can be manipulated in following ways:
- mouse click on the image places light in front of selected point (offset by placement distance.) Placement distance from the selected point can be adjusted using mouse wheel + alt key.
- move light by dragging the mouse pointer while holding left mouse button. Moves light while maintaining placement distance
- rotating mouse wheel while holding control key moves light forward/backward
alignRotation: Duplicate the selected light source. All parameters will be copied to the new one.

queue_dock:
Queue tool allows for rendering a collection of settings files in the background.
While the list of settings files is being rendered, you can continue to work in the main window and also add more settings to the queue.
Methods to manage queue:
- by adding items using Add current settings button
- by editing queue.fractlist file
- by putting files into queue folder and use button Add orphaned
- by adding single settings or lists using command line interface
Temporary settings files are stored in $HOME/.mandelbulber/queue folder and the list is in $HOME/.mandelbulber/queue.fractlist
The queue can be rendered in another instance of Mandelbulber program, as the queue is shared between applications. You can also launch another Mandelbulber from command line interface with -q option. Then this application will watch queue and render automatically all new items.
Result images are saved into $HOME/.mandelbulber/images directory (or another if it's specified in application preferences.)
voxel_greyscale_iterations:
When this option is enabled, the fractal appearance is maintained at all resolutions.
The fractal detail level will be automatically adjusted to match any change of image resolution.
For instance, if the resolution is doubled then the detail level will be reduced by half.
